subject: Attestation workflow + operational erase runbook questions
messages:
From: Claire Ho <claire.ho@intellifin.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: security@intellifin.com
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:12:43 -0800
Subject: Questions on your 'not used for training' assurance + deletion evidence

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Security had a couple of follow-ups before we can move to legal review:

- Can Redwood provide a formal attestation that customer request/production input data is not used to train or improve public models?
- Operationally, what exact artifacts might still exist after a deletion request (e.g., debug snapshots, backups, telemetry) and what are the timelines to fully remove those?
- We also need an explanation of how you handle ephemeral caches (KV/cache) vs. durable logs, and whether any of that could ever be included in model training datasets.

Would appreciate a short summary and any supporting evidence (SOC2, attestation PDF, or an ops runbook). We can then include that in our procurement checklist.

Claire
Claire Ho
Head of Information Security
IntelliFin

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ho <claire.ho@intellifin.com>
Cc: security@intellifin.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 10:03:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on your 'not used for training' assurance + deletion evidence

Hi Claire —

Great questions, thank you. I pulled together a concise summary below and attached a draft attestation and our operational erase runbook for your review. High level: Redwood does not use customer request payloads or customer-hosted documents to train any of our public or internal models. We do keep a small set of telemetry and operational logs for debugging, billing, and compliance; those are governed by distinct retention controls and can be excluded under contract with customer-managed keys or explicit contractual clauses.

Short answers:
- Attestation: attached (redwood_attestation_draft.pdf). This is what we typically provide customers as a signed addendum to the contract.
- Artifacts & timelines: see attached runbook (erase_ops_runbook_v1.docx) and the short matrix below.

Retention/erase summary (operational):
- KV cache / in-memory session data: ephemeral, evicted within seconds to minutes after session close; not written to persistent store.
- Request logs (structured): default retention 90 days for billing/usage; 7 days of high-fidelity traces for hot debugging; beyond 90 days we rotate to a compressed archive that is retained for up to 365 days for legal/billing only.
- Snapshots & debug dumps: created only when debugging incidents and retained for a short window (7–30 days) unless explicitly preserved for an investigation; snapshots are tagged and can be deleted on request.
- Backups: periodic encrypted backups exist for disaster recovery; backups are on a 30–90 day rotation depending on the service tier; we have an operational process to remove customer data from backups over a bounded window after an erase request (see runbook).
- Model training datasets: we do not mix customer request content or uploaded documents into training corpora. Any telemetry used for model improvements is aggregated + sampled and scrubbed for PII; customers can opt-out contractually.

Next steps I propose:
1) If your legal team is comfortable with the draft attestation, we can route it for signature (DocuSign).
2) If you need tighter operational controls (shorter retention, immediate deletion of snapshots), we can add a contract addendum and technical playbook.
3) Mina (cc'd) can follow up with a short technical appendix describing the actual erase command flow and KMS options.

Happy to hop on a quick call with you + security if helpful.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(priyom.das@redwood.com)

Attachments: redwood_attestation_draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB), erase_ops_runbook_v1.docx (DOCX, 120KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, Claire Ho <claire.ho@intellifin.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 11:29:07 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on your 'not used for training' assurance + deletion evidence

Claire / Priyom —

Adding some operational specifics so your security team can assess risk:

- Erase flow: when a tenant-initiated erase is triggered we mark the customer records as "tombstoned" immediately (metadata flag). Tombstoning prevents further serving and ensures any operational reads are blocked. Tombstoned data is then queued for removal from live stores within a 24–72 hour window depending on volume and the tenant's plan.
- Cache & KV: our inference runtime keeps a per-request KV cache in RAM and a short-lived local cache on the serving host. These are flushed on process restart and are not persisted to object storage under normal operation. We never materialize request text into long-term blob storage as part of runtime caching.
- Snapshots/backups: our DR backups are multi-region and encrypted. Removing a record from a snapshot requires a coordinated restore-and-prune process for that backup generation; the runbook describes an SLA window (typically up to 90 days to guarantee full removal from all backup media without impact to availability). For customers requiring faster guarantees we offer an addendum that shortens backup retention and gives a documented workflow for targeted prune.
- Telemetry used for engineering: we collect anonymized metrics and aggregated model telemetry for capacity planning and model regression detection. Any telemetry intended for research is run through an internal anonymization pipeline and aggregated at a high level; per-customer opt-out is supported under contract.
- Evidence & audits: we can provide SOC2 Type II and recent penetration test summaries; the attestation PDF covers the "no training" promise and the legal team can sign a supplemental clause to be appended to the MSA.

If you have a compliance checklist, send it over and I can map each item to an operational control. Happy to prepare a short appendix that our security team will sign off on.

--
Mina Haddad
Director, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
(mina.haddad@redwood.com)

Attachment referenced: log_retention_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, permissions: redact on share)

From: Claire Ho <claire.ho@intellifin.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 14:02:55 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on your 'not used for training' assurance + deletion evidence

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our audit team:

1) Can you confirm whether archived/compressed logs retained beyond 90 days could contain raw request text (we need to know if any plaintext customer data exists beyond 90 days in any storage tier).
2) If we request a ledger of all delete actions for our tenant (with timestamps and operator ids), can Redwood produce that for an audit?
3) For the attestation: will your legal team accept a single-line addendum that explicitly states "Redwood will not use customer request data or uploaded customer files to train models or create model derivatives"?

If yes to all, we can move to legal review and I will also share our procurement redlines.

Claire

From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ho <claire.ho@intellifin.com>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com, security@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 15:47:01 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on your 'not used for training' assurance + deletion evidence

Claire —

Short answers to your audit follow-ups:

1) Archived/compressed logs: by default we do not retain raw request plaintext in long-term archives beyond 90 days. The compressed archives kept for billing/legal purposes are limited to structured metadata and hashed identifiers; any plaintext traces are removed or tokenized prior to archive. If your policy requires zero plaintext in any long-term archive, we can add contractual controls and customer-managed encryption keys to enforce that via our backup prune workflow.

2) Delete ledger: yes — we can produce a machine-readable ledger of delete actions for your tenant that includes timestamp, action type (tombstone, prune from store, backup-pruned), and operator id (system or operator). We will need to scope retention of that ledger per your audit retention requirements.

3) Attestation language: our legal team is generally willing to sign a focused addendum. I’ve asked legal to review the one-line clause you proposed; Mina and I will coordinate on any minor language changes to ensure it is both operationally accurate and contractually enforceable.

Next steps:
- Legal will send a redlined attestation for your review (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-attest-intellifin).
- If you want, we can add a one-hour technical walkthrough with our ops team to demo the erase flow and show the ledger generation.
- Once attestation is accepted, we’ll route the addendum via DocuSign and add the agreed retention/backup tweaks to the SOW.

Thanks — will keep you posted.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(priyom.das@redwood.com)
